summary: Reproduced the explicit NIXL guard for heterogeneous-TP non-MLA SWA state transfer. Current mirror main still has the guard. The ordinary heterogeneous-TP KV path has head-slice transfer planning, but the SWA extra-state path only has whole-item generic transfer, so removing the guard is not a valid fix.

tests.what_was_measured: Actual NixlKVManager.maybe_send_extra dispatch: reproduced non-MLA SWA TP 2-to-4 rejection and independently verified equal-TP non-MLA and heterogeneous-TP MLA accepted boundaries.

tests.command: git fetch origin main; compare the NIXL guard at recorded base and origin/main
tests.what_was_measured: The same unsupported heterogeneous-TP non-MLA SWA guard exists at base 358c163250ad3b1f62939b01ce1314a0a31a0365 and current mirror main bd45cd50ca900dd821f829ca9adfbf9aa3336bda.
Exactly one visible AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 device; insufficient to execute heterogeneous tensor-parallel ranks.

gpu_execution.evidence: Device discovery found one gfx950 GPU, but no GPU kernel or multi-rank transfer was executed; heterogeneous TP cannot be reproduced on one assigned GPU.

remaining_limitations: Only one gfx950 GPU was assigned; heterogeneous TP and multi-rank NIXL transfer were not executable.
GPT-OSS-120B weights were unavailable, so the reported full model and P/D deployment were not run.
The deterministic tiny Llama fixture cannot qualify GPT-OSS hybrid SWA state transfer and was therefore not substituted for the reported architecture.
Supporting this architecture requires a destination-rank-aware SWA head slicing/gather/scatter design across transfer backends, not removal of the capability guard.
